limitations: Public reader is a differential comparator, not an independent semantic oracle. Disagreements require fixture/specification or independent-engine validation before choosing a fix.
Test-side collected rows and public oracle allocations are outside the owned pool. Pool assertions prove tracked cleanup, not process memory.
Core struct vectors intentionally unify field names and fill missing fields with null; applying that contract to JSON/variant objects can change object shape.
Public INT96 conversion and owned wide timestamp decoding disagree for a far-future Spark value; do not truncate the owned value merely to match the public reader.
nextWork: Establish canonical public/query value contracts for dynamic JSON/variant objects versus fixed-schema structs.
Validate timestamp and legacy repeated/map disagreements against independent fixture expectations.
Resolve original unsupported encoding/codec and variant failures; release gate remains failing.

packages/parquet/src/temporal-values.test.ts asserts Date carriers from DATE parser
temporalFollowup.change: Parity comparison canonicalizes Date carriers only; retains timestamp precision/unit, bytes, bigint, object keys, null versus empty, and non-record objects. Seven explicit fixture tests assert documented public Dates and owned timestamps, including output release. No production API changes.

int96Followup.result: Raw dictionary bytes reproduce documented Spark signed-microsecond writer arithmetic. Owned output matches all six rows including null and exact nanoseconds; public and DuckDB each disagree at row 5. Owned output releases to zero.
int96Followup.rootCause: Upstream readPlainInt96 combines a signed low 64-bit word with the high word, allowing sign extension to erase the day word before timestamp parsing. A custom scalar timestamp parser alone cannot recover it.
int96Followup.remaining: Share the correct physical INT96 decoding contract with public and fallback readers; preserve ordinary Julian interpretation and Spark auto selection. No decoder fix or conformance exemption applied.

int96SharedHelpers.change: Scoped and borrowed readPlainValues now share validated INT96 carrier decoding; convertDecodedValues uses the same temporal conversion regardless of allocation scope. Scoped reservation and cleanup remain unchanged.
int96SharedHelpers.validation: 2708 default tests passed, 605 skipped; 25 focused carrier/temporal tests passed; seven temporal tests rerun with independent exact epoch constants passed. TypeScript build passed.
int96SharedHelpers.remaining: Public object reader still calls upstream directly; the public fixture mismatch is not fixed by this shared-helper change.

int96PublicIntegration.change: Pinned hyparquet patch preserves unsigned low words and adds optional physical INT96 parser hook. Public object/column and legacy scan paths select shared ordinary/Spark parser tables from writer metadata. Published package bundles the patched reader and includes its license.
int96PublicIntegration.remaining: Original 18 corpus failures plus JSON shape, map-without-value shape, and legacy repeated null/empty discrepancies remain. Pool accounting limitations elsewhere are unchanged.

jsonObjectContract.change: JSON objects use dynamic map vectors rather than fixed-schema structs. A shared map builder admits map entries before construction for parsed JSON and fallback column normalization. Arrays, nulls, absent keys and explicit null fields retain their distinctions. Public decoded-row normalization defines own properties, including __proto__.
jsonObjectContract.focusedValidation: 17 focused tests passed, including exact/one-byte-short JSON allocation bounds, parse failure rollback, true/ignored HTTP ranges, concurrent cold/warm cache reuse, retained output after cache eviction, repeated gather/concat, and generated nested fixtures at batch sizes 1, 3, 32.
limitations: Native JSON parser/reviver workspace remains outside the parsed-tree allocation model.

Upstream fixture writer toJson drops __proto__ before encoding. Generated readback tests exclude that key; parser and public normalizer tests explicitly exercise it independently. Writer preservation remains an open finding.
Two remaining parity disagreements: map-without-value and unannotated repeated fields. Original 18 corpus failures remain.
jsonObjectContract.tradeoff: Dynamic map entries add explicitly admitted storage versus fixed-schema struct inference. The parser tree and replacement map storage remain conservatively charged together; this is needed to preserve member presence, not a tunable semantic choice.

collectionShapeIntegration.change: Pinned reader recognizes key-only MAP schemas, supplies null values during assembly without constructing a synthetic value column, and distinguishes empty REPEATED leaves from null OPTIONAL values. Capability rejects absent/repeated keys and unknown second fields; key/value schema order is not assumed.

validation.buildLintTypecheck: passed, including final schema capability test

collectionShapeIntegration.remaining: All eleven additional differential disagreements are resolved or independently validated representation differences. The original eighteen failures remain, along with the broader memory audit requirements.

currentRevalidation.conclusion: The release gate still fails. Recent JSON stream and string sizing changes introduce no additional failures in this corpus. No exclusions or assertions changed.

dictionaryExtentInvestigation.finding: The name and comment_col metadata total_compressed_size each omit exactly their 15-byte dictionary-page header. Their declared ends are 451/2593, whereas the last data-page bodies end at 466/2608. Other columns have no shortfall.
dictionaryExtentInvestigation.validation: Unmodified metadata rejects. Correcting only those two metadata extents in the diagnostic restores all 25 rows. All values match DuckDB, comparing binary values with UTF8 bytes from reader strings. Fixture bytes and production code remain unchanged.
dictionaryExtentInvestigation.next: Implement generic bounded page-extent recovery with validated neighboring-column/footer boundaries and admission before extra cloud range reads. Do not globally pad every column, download whole objects, or classify this fixture as an expected rejection. Conformance remains 18 failures until production integration passes.

inspector.contract: Given a validated next-column/footer boundary, inspect bounded page headers for a missing-dictionary-offset column. Return a correction only for exactly one omitted initial dictionary header and the exact declared value count. Empty encoding lists are permitted because this fixture has them; page types provide the proof. Do not mutate metadata or fetch separate page bodies.
inspector.validation: Real fixture proves two 15-byte recoveries. Boundary one byte short, inconsistent value count, and size shortfall not equal to the dictionary header all reject. Already-corrected metadata stays unchanged. Tiny budgets reject at header-probe admission; scopes return to zero.
inspector.integration: Internal inspector only; public/owned readers do not call it yet. No conformance improvement is claimed. Integrating validated physical bounds, owned metadata changes, and cloud transport tests remains required.

productionIntegration.change: Public object/column/vector and owned indexed/cached readers apply proven dictionary extent corrections in private metadata. Source metadata and cached entries are not mutated. Corrected object/array directories are admitted before copying, and header reads use the existing allocation-aware page inspector. Physical bounds come from all column starts and the footer; indexed group owners are released while enumerating those bounds.
productionIntegration.lazyPlanning: Object/vector recovery occurs at the selected row group. Ordinary early exit preserves lazy prefetch; the existing planned-past-window regression passes. Full physical-boundary enumeration is reserved for candidate missing-dictionary-offset metadata.

validation.targeted: 58 reader/lazy-planning/malformed/HTTP checks passed; metadata immutability and scoped copy ownership assertions passed afterward.

productionIntegration.http: Actual external fixture over true 206 and ignored-range 200 responses; indexed auto and cached modes; three concurrent queries at batch sizes 1/3/32 under a 64 MiB shared pool; complete value parity, independently specified nation names and keys, cancellation, zero final reservation usage. Requests remain within file bounds.
productionIntegration.expectationChanges: The historical nation.dict-malformed rejection case is replaced by successful real-fixture HTTP checks, supported by the independent 25-row DuckDB oracle. ARROW-RS-GH-6229-DICTHEADER still rejects, now at physical-boundary validation before its malformed compact header. No conformance exclusion or expected-failure waiver was added.
limitations: The full conformance gate still fails on sixteen other cases.
Specific fixture recovery has HTTP coverage; existing Worker suite passes but does not newly exercise this external fixture via native R2.
Physical-boundary enumeration for anomalous candidates can inspect all row groups; no claim of unchanged malformed-file planning cost.
Remaining decoder/runtime workspace and broader audit allocation gaps are unchanged.

proofReuseAndNativeR2.change: Private recovered row groups carry a scoped projection proof. Repeated batch consumers skip already inspected columns without a process-wide cache or mutations to original metadata. Projection arrays are copied under the allocation scope; requesting another column does not inherit an unrelated proof.
proofReuseAndNativeR2.proofTest: A reader that throws on either slice or sliceOwned proves repeated recovery and narrower projections perform zero reads and allocate no additional reservations. A name-only correction leaves comment_col unchanged; a later comment_col projection inspects and corrects it independently without changing the earlier metadata.
proofReuseAndNativeR2.nativeR2: The Worker test configuration loads the exact external fixture bytes into a test-only binding. Four native-R2 cases cover 64/128 MiB pools and indexed/cached metadata, concurrent owned outputs at batch sizes 1/3/32, output retention, cancellation, complete parity with the corrected public reader, independently specified keys/first-last names, and zero reservations after release. The suite ran all 57 cases without skips.
proofReuseAndNativeR2.limits: This is local workerd/Miniflare native R2 operation with reservation assertions, not deployed-cloud total-heap proof or near-cap workload stress. The conformance checkpoint remains 477 passed and 16 failed from the preceding full run.

typedBinaryVariant.oracle: Vendored cases.json specifies BINARY 0A0B0C0D. Tests assert those bytes independently of public/owned parity.
typedBinaryVariant.cause: The upstream variant decoder treated Uint8Array in typed_value as an encoded variant payload, reading its data bytes as headers. typed_value is already decoded physical binary; encoded payloads belong to value wrappers.
typedBinaryVariant.change: Pinned hyparquet patch preserves typed binary backing without copying or reparsing. The same rule applies to nested array elements. value wrappers continue to parse encoded variant payloads.

validation.defaultScope: Full suite before adding two HTTP tests; the final focused run includes both HTTP tests.

cases: HTTP modes with zero final pool usage
Clean installed package public/owned fixture reads
typedBinaryVariant.remaining: Four decimal variant fixtures require exact high-precision scalar representation; relaxing schema rejection would silently round values. Other remaining failures are ALP, BSON and BROTLI, each through both readers. No exclusions or assertion waivers added. HTTP tests do not establish production Cloudflare heap safety.

independentDecimalOracle.cause: The binary variant decimal decoder converts signed coefficients to Number and multiplies by 10**-scale. Both readers share this path, so parity does not detect lost digits. Shredded high-precision decimals reject earlier, while equivalent binary variants silently round.
independentDecimalOracle.observed: 123456789.987654321 becomes 123456789.98765433 in both readers. Cases 70-73 and 112-115 lose documented digits; cases 26-29 reject.
independentDecimalOracle.gateChange: Sixteen independent decimal assertions compare documented exact spellings without converting expected values to Number. Existing corpus assertions and unsupported-format failures remain. This exposes existing loss; no expected-failure waiver or skip added.
requiredContract: An exact decimal scalar must preserve a signed coefficient and scale across both shredded leaves and binary variants, with shared conversion hooks.

Generic vectors, literals, comparisons, grouping/hash keys, sorting, arithmetic and aggregates need explicit decimal capabilities and consistent numeric coercion; a generic object fallback must not silently change semantics.

Coefficient backing, scale alignment, arithmetic scratch, serialized text and vector directories must be admitted before allocation; huge scales must not trigger unbounded zero padding or powers of ten.
JSON/CSV output must preserve exact digits under a documented representation, without silently converting back to binary64.
Validate primitive and nested values, signed boundaries, scale normalization, null/empty values, budget caps, cancellation, real HTTP/R2 fixtures and clean package distribution.
independentDecimalOracle.scope: Oracle uses memoryStore and vendored fixture documentation. No cloud performance or total-memory claim. Exact-decimal support remains unimplemented; removing the schema precision guard alone is not an acceptable fix.

exactDecimalKernel.status: Internal representation/comparison/formatting implemented; not yet connected to readers or generic execution, and not exported from the package entry point.
exactDecimalKernel.contract: Immutable bigint coefficient with a nonnegative safe-integer scale. Canonical fixed spelling at adjusted exponents -6 through 20 and scientific spelling otherwise. Exact string/JSON conversion; implicit numeric coercion rejects.
exactDecimalKernel.comparison: Compare signs and adjusted exponents, then virtual zero-extended coefficient digits. No powers of ten or scale-sized strings. Same-scale/sign/zero shortcuts avoid formatting entirely.
exactDecimalKernel.allocation: Optional scope admits scalar backing and formatting before allocation. Comparison reserves coefficient strings and releases in finally. Formatting estimate includes slices, mantissa, exponent and output. VM/GC internals and BigInt arithmetic used for forecasts remain separate.

MAX_SAFE_INTEGER scale with constant coefficient-sized workspace

exactDecimalKernel.measurement: For fixed coefficients at scales 4, 1000 and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER, comparison peak is 136 reservation bytes and formatting retains 1036 reservation bytes in every case. Microbenchmark medians are approximately 0.00016-0.00017ms; this is a kernel check, not query/cloud performance.
exactDecimalKernel.remaining: Connect exact decimal capabilities to vectors, readers, generic comparison/hash/sort, arithmetic/aggregates and owned output. Preserve existing low-precision number behavior where required by compatibility. The 30 conformance failures remain unresolved at this checkpoint.

exactDecimalArithmetic.status: Internal add/subtract/multiply kernel implemented; generic vector/operator and reader integration remain outstanding.
exactDecimalArithmetic.contract: Caller must supply MemoryScope. Scale alignment, powers, aligned coefficients, result coefficient and scalar storage are admitted as one stage before arithmetic. Only retained result backing survives stage cleanup. Zero operands avoid needless alignment. Result scale must fit a nonnegative safe integer.
edgeCases: Exact documented 18/19-digit decimal values
Signed addition/subtraction/multiplication with unequal scales
Exact-cap success and one-byte-short rejection
Billion-digit and MAX_SAFE_INTEGER alignment gaps reject with zero peak admission
Same MAX_SAFE_INTEGER scales compute without rounding the size forecast
Zero addition, subtraction/negation and multiplication do not expand scale gaps
Scale overflow preserves existing live reservations
Shared-pool sibling arithmetic rejects while a previous result is retained, then succeeds after release
exactDecimalArithmetic.discoveredDuringTesting: Compute digit growth as coefficientDigits + (resultScale - inputScale); adding the scale before subtracting can round the size forecast near MAX_SAFE_INTEGER. Tests cover equal extreme scales.
exactDecimalArithmetic.remaining: The explicit backing forecast is not a portable bound on native BigInt implementation scratch or delayed GC. Division/rounding semantics, generic decimal vector capabilities, comparisons/hash/sort/aggregates, readers and cloud fixture integration remain. The 30 conformance failures are unchanged.

binaryVariantDecimalIntegration.change: Pinned hyparquet adds an optional decimalFromUnscaled parser hook for binary variant decimal4/8/16 carriers. LakeQL preserves unsafe coefficients as DecimalValue; safe coefficients retain numeric compatibility with correctly rounded scaling. Public decoded-row normalization preserves the scalar class. Owned object/column readers supply scoped parser tables for variant schemas, admitting scalar backing and large-scale formatting scratch before allocation; other schemas reuse shared tables.
binaryVariantDecimalIntegration.boundary: Binary variant coefficients have a format-defined 4/8/16-byte extent and a one-byte scale. This integration does not relax the schema guard for ordinary/shredded high-precision decimal leaves, whose conversion and operator contracts still need integration.

Positive and negative safe-integer representation boundaries

binaryVariantDecimalIntegration.cloudEvidence: Real case-070 fixture passes public/owned reads and exact JSON output over HTTP 206 and ignored-range 200 responses. Local workerd native R2 tests exercise 64/128 MiB shared pools, three concurrent owned queries and a cancelled peer, with per-query pool/4 limits and zero final reservations. This is not production Cloudflare total-heap certification.

binaryVariantDecimalIntegration.remaining: Four shredded high-precision decimal fixtures still reject through both readers; ALP, BSON and BROTLI account for six other failures. Generic decimal expression/order/group/aggregate integration and broader decoder/runtime memory accounting remain open. No tests were waived.

boundedDecimalDiagnostics.change: Rejected decimal values no longer retain byte-carrier backing, malformed object graphs or arbitrary strings in error details. BigInt diagnostic formatting is restricted to signed 128-bit coefficients; larger values use a fixed message before any toString call. Existing physical integer diagnostics remain exact.
edgeCases: An 8-byte invalid carrier aliases a 1 MiB backing buffer; the error contains only carrier type and length.
Malformed object with hostile toJSON is never retained or invoked.
A 1 MiB malformed string is replaced by its type.
Positive and negative million-bit integers reject without invoking BigInt.toString.
Signed 128-bit boundaries retain exact diagnostic text.
Failed scoped scalar conversion releases its reservation.
boundedDecimalDiagnostics.limits: This bounds input-dependent diagnostic payloads, not Error stack/runtime allocation. Shredded decimal integration and the remaining audit requirements are still open.

shreddedVariantDecimals.change: Shared scoped decimal conversion now accepts physical integer and signed big-endian byte leaves inside VARIANT. Pinned hyparquet bypasses binary UTF-8 handling for decimal annotations, preserves nulls, recognizes logical-only DECIMAL annotations, and exposes a scalar predicate so DecimalValue and TimestampValue survive shredded-object assembly.
shreddedVariantDecimals.contract: Schema traversal tracks the outermost VARIANT ancestor in constant additional state. Precision through 38 is admitted for supported physical decimal carriers inside that logical container. Ordinary high-precision nested decimal vectors retain their guard until their numeric execution shape supports exact scalars. Byte carriers strip redundant sign extension without copying, reject empty or more than 16 significant bytes, and admit fixed coefficient workspace before BigInt construction. Scales must be nonnegative safe integers through 38. Scoped result backing is admitted through the same factory as binary variants.
edgeCases: Both signs and signed 128-bit extremes; sign-extended carriers of 16 and 65536 bytes.
Empty and oversized byte carriers, noninteger numbers and invalid scale reject.
Exact capacity succeeds and one-byte-short capacity rejects while releasing coefficient workspace.
Logical-only and converted DECIMAL annotations preserve nullable values.
Decoded decimal and timestamp objects remain scalar through direct and nested shredded wrappers.
A VARIANT sibling cannot relax the ordinary nested decimal schema guard.
All twelve independent documented decimal fixtures preserve exact spelling through public and owned readers; eight additional independent assertions cover formerly rejected fixtures.
shreddedVariantDecimals.cloudEvidence: Cases 026–029 pass public/owned/exact-JSON checks over HTTP 206 and ignored-range 200 responses. Case 028 also passes local workerd native R2 reads with 64/128 MiB shared pools, three concurrent owned queries and a cancelled peer, per-query pool/4 limits, no range cache and zero final reservations. Case 070 binary coverage remains. Clean npm install checks both binary and shredded real fixtures.
shreddedVariantDecimals.limits: The fixture oracle measures tracked reservations and exact output, not CPU speed or production Cloudflare total heap. Native BigInt scratch/GC and broader allocation accounting remain open. Generic decimal expression/order/group/aggregate integration and ordinary high-precision vector integration remain unfinished. No unsupported-codec tests were waived.
